prompt: The client wants to know what is driving its revenue growth. Which takeaway matters most?

options.text: Growth comes from more customers; spend per customer slipped
options.feedback: Right. Customers grew 72% (50k to 86k) and revenue 60% (100 to 160), so revenue per customer fell from about $2,000 to $1,860.

options.text: Revenue growth was 60% in three years, to $160M
options.feedback: True, but it doesn't say what drives the growth: more customers or more spend per customer.

options.text: Spend per customer rose as revenue outpaced customers
options.feedback: On the two axes the lines look alike, but customers grew 72% and revenue 60%, so spend per customer fell.

options.text: Marketing spend brought in the new customers
options.feedback: The chart shows customer numbers, not marketing. That may be true, but nothing here supports it.

explanation: Customers grew 72% (50k to 86k) and revenue 60% (100 to 160), so revenue per customer fell from about $2,000 to $1,860.

extras.proof: Customers grew 72% (50k to 86k) and revenue 60% (100 to 160), so revenue per customer fell from about $2,000 to $1,860.
